title: Unique descent of the canonical affine reverse comparison
statement: Let A,B be commutative rings, φ:B→A, f=Spec(φ), i∈ℤ, with derived scheme-module categories [def-pc-derived-category, def-pc-derived-direct-image]. There is a unique natural isomorphism τ:H^i Rf_*→f_* H^i on D_QCoh(Spec A) whose component at Q(I), for every K-injective complex I with quasi-coherent cohomology, is H^i of the canonical isomorphism Rf_*Q(I)→Q(f_*I), followed by the localization/homology factor, the explicit left exact reverse homology comparison [def-pc-left-exact-homology-comparison], and f_* of the inverse localization/homology factor at I. This determines τ including its inverse by literal equality.

source.place: 0AVW, proof, affine cohomology display; 08D4, bound-one truncation comparison on inverse images of affine opens.

proof.text: On the full subcategory of K-injective complexes form the natural transformation given by the inverse right-derived unit, the target localization/homology factor, the explicit left exact reverse comparison, and the mapped inverse source localization/homology factor. The explicit comparison is natural for chain maps. The restricted localization is a localization at quasi-isomorphisms, so its fully faithful precomposition functor descends this natural transformation to the whole derived category. The map_preimage identity gives precisely the specified formula on every K-injective complex.

Restrict this natural transformation to D_QCoh(Spec A). Its component at a K-injective representative is the specified affineKInjectiveReverseComparison. The middle reverse homology comparison is invertible by the affine K-injective comparison theorem; all other factors are functor images of isomorphisms.

Every derived object admits a K-injective representative. Transport quasi-coherence along its homology isomorphisms and lift the representative isomorphism to the full quasi-coherent subcategory. Naturality transports invertibility from the representative to the original component. Thus the descended natural transformation is a natural isomorphism. For uniqueness, two normalized natural isomorphisms agree at all K-injective representatives; naturality and cancellation along each representative isomorphism give equality of every component, then equality of their hom natural transformations and of the natural isomorphisms.

proof_origin.place: 0AVW, proof, affine cohomology display; 08D4, bound-one truncation comparison on inverse images of affine opens.
proof_origin.note: Descent and uniqueness implemented using fully faithful localization precomposition and K-injective representatives. Affine component invertibility proved in a separate sorry-free module using existing affine derived-equivalence and resolution statements. No exact-family compatibility equation is an input.
